findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. User data is stored unencrypted with the instance and is readable by any process or user on the host via the instance metadata service (169.254.169.254/latest/user-data), and by any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute. These long-lived keys are also committed to source control.

Ingress on TCP 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on an instance that receives a public IP to brute-force and exploitation from any host on the internet. Combined with the credentials in user data, a successful SSH compromise yields AWS API access.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 token-less requests. Because the credentials and any role data are reachable through the metadata endpoint, an SSRF or command-injection flaw in the Apache workload served on port 80 can trivially exfiltrate user_data and metadata.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root volume (which holds the user_data-derived environment and any application data) is created without EBS encryption at rest.

The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data written to the volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted and is exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.

The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and therefore inherits no encryption. Snapshots are independently shareable objects, so an unencrypted snapshot is a durable, easily copied plaintext replica of the volume contents.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This provides no outbound segmentation, enabling a compromised host to exfiltrate data or reach arbitrary command-and-control endpoints.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the instance serves plain Apache HTTP with no TLS listener or load balancer terminating HTTPS, so all traffic to the web host traverses the internet unencrypted.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway means every instance launched here, including the web host, is directly internet-reachable with no NAT or bastion boundary.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the route table that routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway causes any instance in this subnet to be assigned a public IP and be directly exposed to the internet by default.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry containing internal IP addresses, ports and traffic patterns is stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: no public access block or bucket policy
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving it reliant on account defaults to prevent public exposure of network audit data and permitting unencrypted HTTP access.

force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows Terraform to delete the bucket and all flow log objects without emptying it first, and no versioning or object lock protects the logs. This weakens the integrity of security evidence.
